### Managing Products

- The **Products** page has a search bar and collapsible sections for **Fence Types**, **Gates**, **Add-ons**, **Groups**, and **Finishes** so admins do not have to scan one long catalog list.
- To change which fence types appear first, clear the product search and choose **Reorder** in the Fence Types section. Drag products into place or use the up and down arrow buttons, then choose **Save order**. Cancel leaves the saved order unchanged. Organization catalogs keep their own ordering without changing the shared platform library, and the saved order is also used by the Field Estimator.
- On the **Products** catalog page, use **Duplicate** on a fence type or gate to open a pre-filled copy you can adjust and save as a new product.
- When an Org Admin creates or duplicates a fence type, **Location availability** keeps it from being stranded in the organization catalog. If the organization has one location, FenceOS makes the product available there automatically. If it has several, the form starts with all locations and lets you choose specific locations instead. An organization with no locations can still save the product and assign it after location setup.
- To remove an assigned fence-product photo, use the trash button beside its thumbnail. FenceOS clears the photo from the product without deleting the underlying uploaded file or changing saved quote data. Screens and newly generated documents that read the current catalog image will use the normal fallback or placeholder; previously sent emails and downloaded files do not change. An organization cannot remove a shared platform image from an inherited product; upload or remove an organization-specific image instead.
- A fence type's **Base Cost per Section** must include both materials and direct labor for that section. FenceOS adds stain, gates, add-ons, and commission separately, so do not include those again in the base section cost.
- On fence type and gate forms, **Margin (%)** is editable, so you can price from whichever number you think in: type a target margin and FenceOS recalculates the retail price from the base cost, or edit the price or cost and the margin updates on its own. The dollar margin at the current price shows under the field. Entries of 100% or higher are not applied, and leaving the field with an incomplete or invalid entry restores the price you started from. When the cost is zero the margin field is disabled, because no price can satisfy a margin without a cost; margin editing changes only the product's catalog price and never touches saved quotes.
- For custom installation scopes whose economics change job by job, edit an organization-owned fence type and turn on **Price at quote**. You can leave its catalog price and base cost at zero because the estimator will enter both values for each scope. FenceOS automatically turns off **Show on Online Estimator**; Price-at-quote products stay out of public/demo estimators and additional-style choices. If an inherited product needs this setting, edit it in the organization catalog so FenceOS creates the organization-owned version without changing the shared template.
- Org Admins should use **Organization > Products** for full product and gate management. Use the **BOM Setup** button at the top of that page when you need to map products to BOM systems and styles.
- In the Super Admin platform **Products** view, the page now shows the shared template library only. Org-created gates, products, and groups stay inside that org's catalog until you use **Send** or switch into **Viewing as** for that organization.
- Use **Add-ons** on the **Products** page to manage repeatable quote extras such as old fence removal, lifetime warranty, and other flat-price, per-section, or **per-square-foot** upgrades. Choose **Per square foot** only for work an estimator will trace as a treatment area; the saved quote uses the traced, rounded square-foot quantity and the product's quote-time price. Add-on costs are internal; customer quote pages, PDFs, and emails show the customer-facing name, description, quantity, and price only.
- When creating an add-on, **Sort** and **Sold labor hours per unit** start blank so their field labels remain visible. Leaving either one blank saves it as zero.
- When an organization designates an eligible one-hour add-on for labor adjustments, Operator change orders use that product automatically for additional or credited man-hours. FenceOS remains the source of truth for hourly cost and retail. The customer sees the manager-entered work description and total only; the product name and hour quantity stay internal. If no eligible product is designated, Operator shows its manual labor-pricing fallback.
- Wood stain remains a fence finish/pricing setting, not a generic add-on. Use **Finishes** on the **Products** page to review fence products that offer finish choices, and use **Org Settings** for stain pricing and stain color defaults.
- Use **Bulk Upload** on **Products** to upload a CSV of fence types. In the Super Admin platform view, the upload updates the shared template library. In an organization's catalog, the same upload creates or updates org-owned fence types and groups only.
- Use **Catalog CSV** on **Products** to add or update fence types, gates, and add-ons in bulk. Choose **Fence types**, **Gates**, or **Add-ons**, then start from either the **Blank template** (importable columns plus sample rows to replace, with a column guide in the dialog) or **Download current** (your catalog as it is today). Edit the CSV and select it again to preview the exact creates, updates, unchanged rows, groups to be created, and errors before applying anything. The **Gates** section and the **Add-ons** section each also have a direct **Download / upload CSV** button that opens this workflow with that section already selected. Keep `slug` and `catalogId` unchanged for existing rows. A blank `slug` is built from the name, and uploading the same sheet again updates those rows instead of duplicating them.
- Catalog CSV operates in the catalog currently shown. The platform view changes only platform templates. An organization view exports its effective catalog, and changes to inherited rows stay in that organization through the existing override or organization-owned-copy behavior. A pre-change download remains usable for recovery even if the first import turned an inherited row into an organization-owned copy.
- Add-on Catalog CSV stores price and cost in whole cents (`4500` means $45.00; decimals are rejected). In an organization's catalog, an inherited (platform) add-on can only have its price, cost, sold labor hours, customer-quote visibility, checkout-offer setting, field-estimator flag, sort order, and **enabled** changed from the CSV; editing its name, description, category, pricing basis, material, style, or color fails that row. Use `enabled` (not `status`) to turn an inherited add-on off; `status` is the archive control only on organization-owned and platform add-ons and stays read-only on inherited ones.
- The reserved **Old Fence Removal** and **Premium Protection** add-ons always need a price entered in the CSV, never left blank, and Premium Protection also always needs a cost entered; type in the value you want (even if it matches the platform's), because a blank price or cost cell on either row fails the row. Premium Protection's cost cannot be changed by CSV at all. The checkout-offer column can only be turned on for an organization's add-ons when that organization's customer checkout add-ons setting is already turned on.
- Missing CSV columns preserve their current values. A blank cell in a column that is present intentionally clears that optional value when the catalog can represent the clear. An inherited product's group cannot be cleared directly because a blank group override means "keep the platform group"; duplicate that product into the organization catalog first. Products omitted from the file are never deleted or disabled, and an unchanged download re-uploaded without edits performs no writes.
- Fence-type, gate, and add-on files are separate; uploading one kind as another names the columns that belong to the other template. A `groupSlug` that does not exist yet is created for you when you apply, and the preview lists it, so you can rename it later on **Products**. Product images and enabled/disabled state remain read-only in Catalog CSV and should be changed through their focused Products controls. For new products, leave `catalogId`, `source`, `enabled`, and `imageUrl` blank. Prices are whole dollars. Each gate row carries one price, so if a gate costs more at a taller height or wider opening, give each variant its own row and slug (for example `cedar-walk-gate-6ft`). For gates, edit `widthOptions` (separate widths with `|`); its first width becomes the default `widthFeet`. Apply remains disabled until every preview error is fixed; if the catalog changes after preview, preview the file again. Applying is all-or-nothing, so a write failure rolls back the entire file instead of leaving a partial catalog update.
- To edit several fence types at once, select the checkboxes beside the products, choose **Edit selected**, then apply only the fields you want to change. Bulk edit can update material type, product color, style, group, orientation, available heights, map line color, section length, online-estimator visibility, popular flag, finish options, default finish, and benefit text. Inherited platform products inside an org catalog can only receive group and online-estimator visibility overrides unless they are duplicated into org-owned products first.
- Super Admins can now use **Send** on both fence types and gates to copy a template into an organization's catalog without rebuilding it by hand.
- Super Admins can bulk upload fence types from a CSV on the platform **Products** page. The `slug` column is optional; if it is blank or missing, FenceOS generates a unique slug from the product details during upload and reuses that generated slug on repeated imports.
- Fence types can include a short **Product Description** up to 250 characters. This customer-facing copy appears on estimates, quote emails, contracts, PDFs, and downstream catalog exports. Descriptions support simple formatting that renders the same everywhere they appear: wrap text in `**double asterisks**` for **bold**, start a line with `-` for a bulleted list, press Enter for line breaks, and leave a blank line between paragraphs. The description editor includes Bold and Bullet toolbar buttons plus a live preview of the customer-facing result.
- Fence type **Color** can be a single color or a separated list such as `White, Tan`. In Field Estimator quote details, a single color is selected automatically and multiple assigned colors become a line-level color picker.
- When Org Admins edit an inherited fence type's name, material, style, color, description, or other product details, FenceOS saves an organization-owned version of that product and leaves the shared platform template unchanged. The same rule applies to inherited gates: Org Admins can edit gate name, type, widths, heights, material, description, price, cost, group, and sort order from **Organization > Products**. Product and gate slugs stay fixed so existing catalog, location, quote, and integration references keep working.
- On an organization's **Products** page, Org Admins can also use **Duplicate** on fence types and gates. That creates an org-owned copy you can customize without changing the inherited template.
- Gate products can list multiple available widths, such as `8, 10, 12`, without creating separate gate products or separate gate prices. The first width is the default, and reps can pick the installed opening from the gate editor in Field Estimator.
- Fence and gate product height fields use **feet**: enter a comma-separated list such as `4, 4.5, 5, 6`. Use `4.5` for a 54-inch fence. Finish decimal entries before saving: `4.` stays visible while typing but cannot be submitted. Explicit units such as `54"`, `54in`, or `6ft` also work and save as feet. Gate products use their first height as the default; reps can choose the installed height from the gate editor in Field Estimator, and it appears on quote details, customer quote pages, PDFs, and quote emails. Widths and section lengths keep their labeled units.
- Gate products can also include a short **Product Description**. This is useful for custom gates and appears with the gate line on Field Estimator quote details, customer quote pages, PDFs, quote emails, and accepted quote copy emails. Gate descriptions support the same formatting as fence type descriptions: bold, bulleted lists, line breaks, and paragraphs, with the same editor toolbar and preview.
- For every fence type shown online, open its Product Admin form and choose the exact **Single gate product** and **Double gate product** under **Online estimator gate pricing**. The estimator uses that mapped product's current selling price. If a requested gate is not mapped, the customer sees **Price confirmed onsite** and the gate adds $0. Do not guess mappings from product names or materials. Before enabling this pricing release, verify every online style, including that **Privacy White Vinyl** points to the current **$800 Single Vinyl Gate** product.
- When a lead with a mapped online-estimator gate is opened in Field Estimator, FenceOS adds it as a standalone gate and re-reads its current tenant catalog price. The amount shown to the customer remains in the lead snapshot for reference but never overrides Field Quote pricing.
- If a Super Admin uses the **Viewing as** organization switcher, the **Products** page works inside that organization's catalog. New products, edits, and duplicates stay in that org, and platform-only actions like bulk upload and push-to-org are hidden while you are in that mode.
- On **Locations**, the product checklist now comes from the selected organization's live catalog instead of the global library. Use **Enable All Org Products** to turn on the full org catalog for a location, or use **Enable Group** inside a product group to turn on a whole group at once. Public estimates use the exact Product Admin catalog price; older saved location prices are labeled as legacy and ignored, and can be cleared from the location editor.

### How product BOM links work

FenceOS does not guess which BOM recipe to use from a display name alone. Each FenceOS fence type must be mapped explicitly.

- Open the relevant fence product and choose the matching **Fence System** and **BOM Style**.
- Optionally choose a default variant and one of the style's supported heights, then set the wood gate build system and notes when applicable.
- Quotes only generate a full BOM when the fence types used in the drawing have matching BOM template coverage.
- Gates require an explicit type and width from the drawing. Wood mappings that select **Insta Gate** or **Wood Frame** require an exact assembly for that family, style, installed height, width, and type; FenceOS does not silently substitute a 4-foot single gate or another family.
- If a quote has enough coverage for fence and post materials but has incomplete gate details or is missing an exact gate material assembly, Operator shows the BOM as **Mixed** and keeps the generated fence/post rows visible for review. **Mixed** and **Failed** BOMs are never order-ready. Correct the drawing or catalog, or add reviewed manual supplement items, before ordering.
- A straight, continuous junction between two drawn segments uses one line post. Corner posts are used where the fence turns, end posts where a run physically stops, and gate posts at gate openings.
- Guided **Review catalog and mappings** checks selected-scope readiness, global catalog validity, sample takeoff quantities, stored-versus-draft entity counts, and the exact server-authoritative mapping diff. **Confirm catalog and mappings publish** stores both datasets in one transaction. Advanced Editor keeps its catalog-focused **Review & Publish** action for expert repair.
- FenceOS publishes against the catalog revision captured by that preview. If another window changes the catalog first, FenceOS makes no replacement, keeps the local edits intact, and asks for **Re-run Preview**.
- Validation failures stay beside **Review & Publish** as an itemized list with the affected product, assembly, or other catalog row. Correct the named rows and choose **Retry**, or use **Repair known catalog defects** when FenceOS can apply the BidRight chain-link height and duplicate-gate correction; the draft is not cleared.
- After **Confirm Publish** completes, the structured catalog and its row counts remain visible; the confirmation reports how many mappings were preserved or dropped, and a browser refresh is not required.
- Publishing the advanced catalog preserves saved product BOM links when the referenced BOM system and style IDs still exist in the saved catalog. If a catalog edit removes or renames those IDs, remap the affected products against the current system and style rows.
